messages:
sam: Heads up: our Android sample shows a retry storm when token refresh runs. 401 -> refresh -> still 401 -> multiple retries until WorkManager times out. Anyone seen this pattern?

lia: yep. Quick check: is your TokenAuthenticator calling the token endpoint with the same OkHttpClient? that causes reentrancy.

sam: ah we are using the same client. sample snippet: 
```kotlin
OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .authenticator(TokenAuthenticator())
  .addInterceptor(AuthInterceptor())
  .build()
```
TokenAuthenticator does a Retrofit call to /oauth/token synchronously.

omar: that's the root cause. Authenticator invoked -> refresh call uses same client -> 401 on refresh -> authenticator invoked again -> loop. Fix by using a dedicated refresh client without authenticator.

lia: also recommendation: in authenticate() return a new Request with the header so follow-up doesn't depend on interceptors, and avoid disk IO on network threads by using an in-memory token cache.

sam: any quick code pattern we can ship in samples?

omar: minimal: create refreshClient = OkHttpClient.Builder().authenticator(null).callTimeout(8, TimeUnit.SECONDS).build() and use that inside TokenAuthenticator. Also short-circuit authenticate for token endpoint paths.

lia: add a CI test with MockWebServer simulating 401 for refresh to ensure no recursion. We had a flaky support ticket causing a bunch of noise.

sam: perfect. I'll update the sample app and open an MR. thanks!

build-bot: created MR #4510 updating android sample and adding TokenAuthenticator example (https://git.internal/redwood/mr/4510)
